articles.headline: Obituary (John W. Whitely)
articles.author: Joseph Cathcart
articles.summary: The noontide eclipse, how solemn and impressive an appeal to man to contemplate the power and majesty of the Creator; but more solemn and more impressive is the appeal when youth falls in its bloom, the noontide eclipse of life. Such was the case of the late John W. Whitely, whose life elicited esteem and friendship. (No place is given.)

articles.headline: Rejoicing in Our City
articles.summary: Last Monday was a day of general rejoicing in our city, among both the white and colored portions of the community. When the news was received, and the Old State House Bell began to peal forth its thundering tones, the people generally laid aside work of every description, in order to share the common joy. In the evening occurred a grand illumination. This also was shared by the American citizens of African descent; and the Institute for Colored Youth, the rooms of the Delmonico Assembly, and several other places of gathering of the colored folks, were beautifully illuminated.

articles.headline: The Union Victories
articles.summary: Steady and ever onward has been the march of the Union army since its command was intrusted to Lieutenant-General Grant, until, at last, that cry is heard, "Richmond is ours!" To the colored troops, who were the first to enter the doomed city, let all praise be given. History will record the fact that the black man, whose services were at one time refused by the Government, struck the death-blow, and planted the dear old flag where for nearly four years has hung the rebel rag.

articles.headline: A Great Disaster (Bethel A. M. E. church at Penningtonville burned)
articles.summary: We learn from Rev. J. V. Pierce, of the Penningtonville circuit, that on Friday, March 24th, some villain fired the Bethel A. M. E. church at the above-named place. This is a great disaster, as much labor and expense have been incurred in erecting the same. The edifice was completed, with the exception of the plastering, and arrangements had been made for its dedication, which was to have taken place on the first Sabbath in May.

articles.headline: Our Colored Capitalists
articles.summary: It is with great pleasure and eminent satisfaction that we learn of the recent movements of our moneyed men toward forming banking associations. Already we hear of a bank with colored men as officers and directors in New Orleans, and last week several prominent colored men of extensive means and experience in financial affairs, formed themselves into a National Banking Institution. What say the moneyed men of color in our own city? Shall Philadelphia be backward in this great movement?

articles.summary: Mr. Editor: Allow me for the first time, since my arrival at Camp William Penn, to occupy a portion of your columns. articles.headline: From Camp Wm. Penn
articles.author: A. H.
articles.summary: Chelton Hills, Pa., April 6th, 1865. Mr. Editor: I beg your indulgence for intruding upon your columns so soon again. On last Saturday evening, we had a very entertaining homespun lecture, from a colored woman, known as Harriet Tubman. It was the first time we had the pleasure of hearing her. She seems to be very well known by the community at large, as the great Underground Rail Road woman.

articles.headline: Richmond Captured
articles.summary: Lee has surrendered to the Union forces at last. This good news caused great rejoicing throughout the country. For the past week Philadelphia has represented a grand carnival more than the sober-sided Quaker City it is wont to be. We hope that we shall not have cause to regret our rejoicing by some proclamation or other act of our law makers, in regard to the most loyal race of people of which the government can boast.

articles.headline: Prejudice Not Yet Dead
articles.summary: We are sorry that the colored troops and their noble leader were prevented from being the first to enter Richmond. They were in the advance, but were ordered to halt till the arrival of the white troops, who were then given the advance. This was wrong; those who win should wear the laurels.

articles.headline: The Minutes of the Pennsylvania Equal Rights League
articles.author: Wm. Nesbit
articles.summary: April 11, 1865. Mr. Editor: Please permit me to inquire through the columns of the Recorder, why is it that the Minutes of the Pennsylvania Equal Rights Convention, which assembled in Harrisburg, Pa., Feb. 8th, 1865, have never yet been published. I subscribed for a number of copies, and am willing to increase the number, and pay for them in advance, if that will forward the movement. Will the Publishing Committee please let us know the hindering cause?

articles.summary: I cannot write, my heart's too full of grief, / Because the dastard's hand has slain our honored Chief. / Him whom the nation loved, it now must mourn. (Unsigned; dated Philadelphia, April 15, 1865.)

articles.headline: Our Domestic Correspondence (Amityville, N. Y.: speech demanding equal access to the street cars)
articles.summary: Amityville, N. Y., April 15, 1865. Mr. Editor: On the 14th of last month the colored folks of our town held a general mass meeting. We expected several distinguished speakers, including Rev. R. H. Cain, of Brooklyn. The speaker reported said: 'we do demand of the American government civil, religious and political equality, that we may enter the street cars of our most populous cities, without being invited to the front of the car to take a seat at the feet of the driver.' (Out of town; no Philadelphia persons. Parts of the letter and its signature are illegible.)

articles.headline: Our National Sacrifice
articles.summary: The joy of the nation has suddenly been changed to mourning. Abraham Lincoln, the man whom the American people had for a second time chosen for their leader, and placed at the helm of the ship of State, has fallen a martyr to his country. Treason, in its death struggle, has dyed its hands in the blood of the Chief Magistrate of the Republic.

articles.headline: Letter from Richmond
articles.author: Garland H. White
articles.summary: City Point, Va., April 12th, 1865. Mr. Editor: I have just returned from the city of Richmond; my regiment was among the first that entered that city. I marched at the head of the column, and soon I found myself called upon by the officers and men of my regiment to make a speech, with which, of course, I readily complied. A vast multitude assembled on Broad street, and I was aroused amid the shouts of ten thousand voices, and proclaimed for the first time in that city freedom to all mankind.

articles.headline: Notice (Elizabeth James against Samuel Hackey)
articles.author: Elizabeth James
articles.summary: Philadelphia, April 20, 1865. The reports circulated by Samuel Hackey [VERIFY] are infamous slanders. It was, evidently, his own choice to live with his children, so that he might enjoy the benefit of their property, and he also robbed my children of the power to administer on Gracy Rodgers' estate. When called before Bishop Waters, of the A. M. E. Church, to answer for renting the house and leaving the family without shelter, he gave, as an excuse, his pretended failing sight. Rev. L. Lee, and Rev. D. Thomas are witnesses of this fact.

articles.headline: Obituary: B. F. Brown, superintendent of Macedonia Sabbath School, Camden
articles.author: Parnell
articles.summary: Dear Recorder: I am about to inform your many readers of the very sad loss of our beloved and faithful friend and superintendent, B. F. Brown. A great man has fallen, and in the Macedonia Sabbath School a link of chain has been broken; the Sabbath School army has lost its general who, for the last six years, had so faithfully led it. Brother Brown leaves a dear wife and a number of relatives. Signed Parnell, Camden, N. J., April 1[9]th, 1865.
people: deceased; superintendent of Macedonia Sabbath School, Camden, N. J., for six years

articles.headline: Died (Frankford; Fair Haven, N. J.)
articles.summary: Died, at Frankford, on Saturday, April 1st, 1865, Mr. Henry Jeffers [VERIFY], in the 7[?]th year of his age. His funeral sermon will be preached on Sunday, May 7th, at the A. M. E. Bethel Church, Frankford. Also: died at Fair Haven, N. J., Emeline Jamison [VERIFY], a member of A. M. E. Bethel Church.

articles.headline: Letter from Rev. J. C. Gibbs
articles.author: J. C. Gibbs
articles.summary: Wilmington, N. C., April 15, 1865 [VERIFY day]. Mr. Editor: I arrived safely in Newbern on the eighth day after my departure from Philadelphia, being detained in New York four days waiting for a steamer. Sections follow on the refugees and their condition, the schools, the churches and the Presbyterian church; he has charge of the Second Presbyterian Church of Wilmington and has gathered a congregation of three or four hundred persons, both black and white.

articles.headline: Great Exhibition of the A. M. E. Zion Mission Sabbath School
articles.summary: To be given on next Wednesday Evening, the 10th instant, at the Zion Church, in Seventh street below Dickerson. We hope that our citizens will encourage and sustain Rev. Brother Winder, the pastor over the school, in his praiseworthy efforts. Let the house be filled on the evening in question.

articles.headline: Last Quarterly Meeting in Bethel Church
articles.summary: Last Sabbath was the occasion for the last Quarterly Meeting for Bethel church, (for this year,) of which Rev. William Moore is now the pastor. Brother Moore has had quite a revival during the last month or so, in his church, and a good number have professed a hope in Christ Jesus the Lord. On last Friday night the General Class met, and on Monday night the sacred ordinance of Love Feast was observed.

articles.headline: Our Correspondence somewhat interesting (Rev. J. C. Gibbs of the Seventh street Presbyterian church)
articles.summary: We refer our readers to Rev. H. M. Turner's letter, chaplain in the U. S. Army, from our old home, or near it, Raleigh, N. C. We have also received a very interesting letter from Rev. J. C. Gibbs, of the Seventh street Presbyterian church, (colored,) of this city. We refer our readers to his letter on the first page of our paper.
people: of the Seventh street Presbyterian church (colored), Philadelphia (Rev.); now in Wilmington, N. C.

articles.headline: Conferences
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Annual Conference of the A. M. E. Church will meet in this city on the 13th of this month. Charleston, S. C.: this Conference will be re-organized by Bishop Payne, assisted by other ministers of the A. M. E. Church, as soon as practicable. The New York Conference will meet on the 10th of June [VERIFY day]; the New England Conference will also meet on the same day.

articles.headline: Institute for Colored Youth
articles.summary: The thirteenth Annual Commencement of the above named Institute took place on last Thursday, and continued till Friday night. This is one of the best schools in the city, and Professor Bassett and his corps of teachers deserve great credit for the proficiency to which they have, through great exertion, brought it.

articles.headline: Notice: Philadelphia Annual Conference; annual and missionary sermons at Bethel
articles.author: A. W. Wayman
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Annual Conference of the A. M. E. Church will meet in the Union Church, Coates street, Philadelphia, Penna., on Saturday, May 13th, 1865. The annual sermon to the Conference will be preached on Monday afternoon, May 15th, at 4 o'clock, by Rev. Henry Davis. The Missionary sermon on Thursday afternoon, May 18th, at 4 o'clock, by Rev. Joshua A. Woodlyn. These services will take place in Bethel Church on Sixth street. May 1st, 1865.
people: to preach the Missionary sermon (Rev.; printed Woodlyn)

articles.summary: James H. Teagle's first Grand Concert will take place on Monday evening, May 8th, at Concert Hall. The two grand pianos used upon this occasion will be procured from Chickering & Sons. The following named artists will participate in the entertainment: Madam Brown, A. S. articles.headline: Notice: "We mourn, our Chief has fallen" (Fair of the Ladies' Union Association postponed until the 15th of May)
articles.summary: On account of our great national calamity the Fair of the Ladies' Union Association will be postponed until the 15th of May. The tickets already issued will be good for that time. The Fair will continue two weeks. By order of the President. S. Lizzie Brown, Sec'y. P. S. The above named Association return their thanks to the Ladies' Union Association of Harrisburg, for their donation of $40; also, to Miss Amelia Williams, for $60, collected in Harrisburg. Miss E. Mills, President. S. L. Brown, Secretary.

articles.author: T. Gould
articles.summary: The Lord willing, the corner stone of the new A. M. E. Church, at Eversham, New Jersey, will be laid on Thursday, the 18th day of May, 1865, exercises to commence at 2 o'clock, P. M. Bishop Wayman and other prominent ministers of the gospel are expected to be present on the occasion. We would like to raise $100 on the occasion. T. Gould, Minister in charge.

articles.headline: Monument to President Lincoln
articles.summary: We copy the following from the Anglo-African, and heartily approve of the proposition. It is but just to the memory of the martyred hero that the colored Americans should do something to perpetuate the name of one who sacrificed every thing, even life itself, in defending the rights of down-trodden humanity. The letter of M. R. Delany, Major 104th Regt. U. S. C. T. (Charleston, S. C., April 20th, '65), proposes a one cent contribution from every individual of the race and names as common Treasurer Rev. Stephen Smith, Philadelphia.
people: of Philadelphia (Rev.); proposed by M. R. Delany as common Treasurer of the Lincoln monument fund

articles.headline: Bishop Campbell's Arrival
articles.summary: Bishop Campbell arrived here from California, on last Monday evening, the 15th inst. The Bishop made his appearance in the Conference room, on Tuesday morning, quite unexpectedly. He is looking remarkably well, indeed.

articles.headline: Obituary: Rev. Frederick T. Hall, of Union A. M. E. Church
articles.author: J. W. Randolph
articles.summary: Died, at his late residence, 1318 Callowhill street, April 9th, 1865, Rev. Frederick T. Hall, in the triumphant hope of a blessed immortality. The deceased was for many years a member of the A. M. E. Church, Union. He seemed willing to devote his time and talent in obedience to his holy vocation. He died of cancer of the face, in the 71st year of his age.
people: deceased (Rev.); of 1318 Callowhill street; member and preacher of Union A. M. E. Church; died April 9, 1865, in his 71st year

articles.headline: Obituary: Benjamin F. Brown, of Camden
articles.author: C. E. P.
articles.summary: Camden, May 1st, 1865. Died, March 29th, 1865, Mr. Benjamin F. Brown, the teacher of the Public school, and Superintendent of the Sabbath school of the Macedonia Church, to which he belonged. A great and good man has fallen. An immense concourse of people attended the funeral; the entire public seemed to share the grief of the widow.
people: deceased; teacher of the Public school and Superintendent of the Sabbath school of Macedonia Church, Camden; died March 29, 1865

articles.headline: Rev. J. B. Reeve
articles.summary: It gives us more than usual pleasure to say that Rev. J. B. Reeve, of our city, has the honor of being one of the first, if not the first, colored man ever elected as delegate to the General Assembly of the Presbyterian Church. Mr. Reeve has, since he has been pastor of Central Presbyterian Church, greatly endeared himself to our citizens, and is considered one of the ablest divines in our midst.
people: pastor of Central Presbyterian Church (Rev.); elected alternate delegate to the New School Presbyterian General Assembly

articles.headline: A Visit to the Old Folks' Home
articles.summary: On Saturday evening last, Conference visited the Old Folks' Home, on Front street, between Spruce and Pine. This Institution, which has been established for the purpose of taking care of the aged colored people, is under the management of a white and colored Board of Directors. We were kindly received by brother Morris Hall, and the matron, who is a white woman.
people: received the Conference at the Old Folks' Home, Front street between Spruce and Pine (brother)

articles.headline: Sabbath School Anniversary
articles.summary: The anniversary of the Sabbath schools connected with the different churches in the city, which took place on Monday last, the 22d inst., in the Bethel church, was attended with great success. Addresses were made by Revs. Stephen Smith, Turpen, and Woodlyn. Dr. Armstrong also made a short speech, after which he presented a splendid silk banner to the Sabbath school class which had collected the most Missionary money; the infant class of Bethel Church, under the charge of Miss Esther Armstrong, carried off the prize.
people: in charge of the infant class of Bethel Church Sabbath school (Miss)

articles.headline: Notice: whereabouts of William Johnson, Christopher Carter and Elias Harris
articles.author: Annie Jackson
articles.summary: Can any one inform me of the whereabouts of Mr. William Johnson, Christopher Carter, or Elias Harris, from Washington, D. C., who left there, on Saturday, the 13th inst., for Philadelphia, and were going thence to Boston, Mass. Having lost the card they left with me, I cannot tell where to find them. Any information in respect to them will be very thankfully received at No. 612 Locust street, opposite Washington Square.

articles.headline: Indiana and Missouri Conferences
articles.author: J. P. Campbell
articles.summary: The ministers and members of the Indiana Conference are hereby notified, that the Annual Conference, for this District, will be held in the city of Springfield, State of Illinois, commencing at the hour of 9 o'clock, A. M., on Saturday, August 12th, 1865. J. P. Campbell, Presiding Bishop. Philadelphia, May 24th, 1865. A second notice calls the Missouri Conference at New Orleans.

articles.headline: Meeting of the South Carolina Conference
articles.summary: We copy the following report of the proceedings of the above named Conference from the columns of the Charleston Courier. We are much pleased and gratified to know that the Courier has made such full and favorable notice of each day's proceedings. Our special thanks are due to Rev. James Lynch for sending us a copy of the report.

articles.headline: Correction. A False and Ignorant Issue taken against the African Methodist Episcopal Church, and a Correction thereof
articles.summary: There seems to have been a false issue taken, either through malice or ignorance, in regard to the shade of color or hue that constitutes and is to constitute the membership of the African Methodist Episcopal Church. We stand here, at the head of the Church paper, to advocate and assert her rights as an Evangelical Church.

articles.headline: A Tardy Jury
articles.summary: On last Thursday, 25th inst., five old colored residents of this city were returning from their day's work, (cleaning a load of carpets,) and when crossing the corner of 15th [VERIFY] and Washington Avenue met with a painful accident, by which two of the number lost their lives. It appears that a locomotive belonging to the Phila. W. and B. R. R. was running up and down the track with no cars attached.
people: survivor; 'well known in our midst'; jumped from the wagon

articles.headline: At Bethel Church
articles.summary: Rev. William Offer, who intends sailing for California shortly, will preach in Bethel church on Sabbath next, at 3 P. M. Go and hear him.

articles.headline: Hurst St. Wesley Church
articles.summary: Divine service will be held in this church as usual, three times a day, the good Lord permitting. We shall preach a sermon on Sabbath next, with Divine permission. The subject chosen is, 'Who comforteth us in all our tribulation?'

articles.headline: The Colored Lincoln Monument
articles.summary: The colored people intend erecting an Educational Monument to the memory of Abraham Lincoln, to be located in Washington, and known as such. The officers who have been selected are as follows: President, Rev. H. H. Garnet. Vice Presid't, James Wormley. Rev. Stephen Smith, Treasurer. Walker Lewis, Assistant. Mr. Lewis A. Bell, Recording Secretary. William J. Wilson, Corresponding Secretary.

articles.headline: Personal
articles.summary: Rev. Dr. A. T. Wood, of the Indiana Conference, arrived in our city, last Sabbath morning. He came to our residence while we were engaged in family devotion. He preached a very fine discourse on Sabbath morning, in Bethel Church, and in the afternoon in Wesley Church.

articles.headline: The South Carolina Conference
articles.summary: It will be seen that this Conference has progressed finely, and exerted a wonderful influence in the city of Charleston. But we are sorry to see the Rev. Mr. Lewis, of the Methodist Episcopal Church, behave the way he does, if our correspondent be correct in his statement.

articles.headline: Twenty-Fourth Regiment
articles.summary: We have received several letters from some of our brave boys in the 24th Regiment, and our prayers are, that they may succeed well, and that their officers may treat them according to the rules of military regulations.

articles.headline: A First-Class Lodging and Boarding House
articles.summary: Mrs. Anne E. Foster, formerly of Baltimore, but now of this city, has just opened a first-class boarding house at No. 1733 Addison street, Philadelphia. Persons passing through our City of Brotherly Love, as well as our permanent residents, will find every accommodation at this establishment.
people: boarding-house keeper, No. 1733 Addison street (Mrs.; the ad on page 3 prints 'Mrs. Ann E. Foster')

articles.headline: Bishop Wayman's Address. To the members of the Philadelphia Annual Conference on the 23d day of May, 1865
articles.summary: Dear Brethren: It is usual for the presiding officer to deliver an address at the opening of the Conference, but I have deferred what I have to say until the close. Twenty years ago, I stood at the altar of this Conference, and took upon me the vows of an itinerant preacher. There are but two travelling preachers now present, who were members of the Philadelphia Conference then.

articles.headline: Death of Mr. Thomas Hamilton, of the Anglo-African (letter)
articles.author: J. P. C.
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: I have to announce to you the sad intelligence that Mr. Thomas Hamilton, late of the Anglo-African, and brother of Mr. Robert Hamilton, the respected editor of that paper, departed this life yesterday morning, Monday, May 29th, 1865, after a short illness of one week and one day's confinement to his room.

articles.headline: Sermon by Bishop Campbell. 'The War and Its Issues'
articles.summary: Report of a lecture by Bishop Campbell on the war and its issues at the Powell street African M. E. church (San Francisco), reprinted from a California paper; it runs over to page 3. There the Bishop says colored people are now allowed to testify in the courts and, in Washington and Alexandria, to ride in the street cars; he believed they had been allowed that privilege here (San Francisco) by Judge Pratt's decision.

articles.headline: Letter from Lieutenant-Colonel Trippe
articles.author: Lieutenant-Colonel Trippe
articles.summary: A letter from Camp Casey commending the young men enlisted in Philadelphia and trained at Camp William Penn. 'There is Sergeant Stephen F. R. Burdy [VERIFY], Sergeant Simpson, and William H. Rox [VERIFY]. All of these named gentlemen have proved themselves to be men and soldiers in every respect by their praiseworthy efforts to elevate their race.' They are engaged in teaching school and instructing the uneducated. Signed Lieutenant-Colonel Trippe, Commanding 24th Regt. U. S. C. T.; Chas. H. Potter, Acting-Adjutant.

articles.summary: The Indiana Annual Conference will meet on the third Saturday in August, in Springfield, Illinois. The Bishop wishes us to say, that he published in the Recorder that the Conference would meet at an earlier date. The Bishop's Visit: By divine permission, the Bishop will visit Cincinnati, last Sabbath in June; Louisville, Ky., first Sabbath in July; Richmond, Ind.; Indianapolis; Terre Haute; Chicago; Bloomington, Ills., second Sabbath in August.

articles.headline: Notice for the Indiana District
articles.author: Jabez P. Campbell
articles.summary: I will visit the following charges on my route to the Indiana Annual Conference, upon the following days, viz: Louisville, Kentucky, on the first Sabbath in July; Richmond, Indiana, on the 16th of July; Indianapolis, Indiana, on the 23d of July. Signed Jabez P. Campbell, Presiding Bishop. Philadelphia, Pa., May 31, 1865.

articles.headline: The Ohio and Baltimore Conferences
articles.summary: We are sorry to say that we have not had a single copy of the Minutes of the Ohio Annual Conference, notwithstanding our request to receive it. The Baltimore Conference, or the District Book Steward, has failed, up to the time of our writing, to send us a copy.

articles.headline: A Wide Mistake
articles.summary: We are continually receiving advertisements for insertion in our paper, but they are not accompanied by a single dollar. We cannot publish a paper for nothing, and we hope that persons who wish to advertise, will hereafter send the money with their advertisements.

articles.headline: Address to the Mayor of Philadelphia
articles.summary: By special request we publish the following address to his Honor, the Mayor of our city, which is an evidence of the loyalty of the colored people. To Alexander Henry, Mayor: We, the colored citizens of Philadelphia, and members of the Union Baptist Church, located in Minster St., between Lombard and Pine Sts., above Sixth street, assembled in our place of worship on Thursday last, the 1st of June, 1865, in compliance with the Proclamation of Andrew Johnson, President of the United States, for the observance of the obsequies of our late and lamented President.

articles.headline: Letter from Pittsburg: conduct of Philadelphia young men
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: We are sorry to expose any body to the public, but the conduct of some of your Philadelphia young men is too scandalous to be passed by unnoticed. William Dement [VERIFY], James Brooks, and Alexander Brown, of your city, came here, and boarded with us some time, and then slipped off without paying us for their board. Signed, proprietors (firm name unreadable), Pittsburg, Pa.

articles.headline: Notice: Quarterly Meetings of Attleborough Circuit
articles.summary: The Quarterly Meetings of Attleborough Circuit will be held as follows: June 17th and 18th, Buckingham Mountain; July 8th and 9th, Newhope; July 15th and 16th, Attleborough. T. Gould, Elder. J. P. Jay [VERIFY], Minister in charge.

articles.headline: Snow Hill Circuit
articles.summary: The Quarterly meetings of the Snow Hill circuit will be held as follows: Snow Hill, on Sunday, June 10th; Milford, Sunday, June 17th, and Jordantown, Sunday, June 24th. A. Till [VERIFY], Elder.

articles.headline: Notice: Quarterly Meeting of the Macedonia Station, South Camden
articles.summary: The Quarterly Meeting of the Macedonia Station, Spruce Street, South Camden, will take place on the 18th of June. G. E. Boyer [VERIFY], Minister in Charge.

articles.headline: Notice: Unity Lodge, G. U. O. of O. F.
articles.summary: We call the attention of our citizens to the advertisement of Unity Lodge, G. U. O. of O. F., in another column, announcing a grand anniversary demonstration, to come off at Sansom Street Hall, on Wednesday evening, the 14th inst. Tickets can be had of Mrs. James W. Brown, No. 1008 [VERIFY] Shippen street, who is one of the committee. Buy your tickets from Mrs. Brown; they are only 75 cents each.
people: member of the committee; tickets, Shippen street

articles.headline: Pennsylvania State Equal Rights Convention
articles.summary: The Minutes of the Pennsylvania State Equal Rights Convention, and Constitutions for State and subordinate Leagues, are now ready for sale, at the following rates: Minutes, $20.00 per hundred, 25 cents per copy; Constitutions, 5 cents per copy. Orders accompanied by the cash and postage, should be sent to Jacob C. White, Jr., Secretary of State League, 717 Lombard St., Philadelphia, Pa.
people: Secretary of State League, 717 Lombard St. (printed 'Jacob C. White, Jr.')

articles.headline: Acknowledgments
articles.summary: Cambridgeport, Mass., Maria A. Hatton, $1.50; Georgetown, D. C., Rev. J. Starbert; Louisville, Ky.; Port Deposit, Md., Rev. W. H. Hopkins, 6. (No Philadelphia names.)

articles.headline: Odd Fellows' Grand Demonstration. The Twenty-First Anniversary of Unity Lodge, No. 711
articles.summary: Odd Fellows' Grand Demonstration. The Twenty-First Anniversary of Unity Lodge, No. 711, of the Grand United Order of Odd Fellows, and of the introduction of the Order into the State of Pennsylvania, will be celebrated at the Sansom Street Hall, on Wednesday Evening, June 14, 1865. Tickets, 75 cents. To be had of the Committee.

articles.headline: Our National Fast
articles.summary: Never in the history of Philadelphia, has there been such a general or appropriate observance of a national fast day, as was noticed yesterday throughout our city. Business was entirely suspended. There was preaching in all the churches in the morning, and the invitation of the Committee of the Lincoln Monument Fund, asking that a collection be taken in the several churches, was read.

articles.headline: Greytown, Central America
articles.summary: Some twelve years since, a colored preacher of Philadelphia, felt moved to go to Greytown and preach the gospel to the people. He left all, and procured a lease of a lot, erected a church building and a dwelling, and has since been the recognized pastor of the people composing the Protestant congregation. His name is Benjamin Smith. After a few years residence in Greytown, he went to Canada and procured orders, under the authority of the Canadian Conference.
people: colored preacher of Philadelphia; pastor at Greytown, Central America

articles.headline: Meeting of the South Carolina Conference
articles.summary: We copy the following report of the proceedings of the above named Conference from the columns of the Charleston Courier. We are much pleased and gratified to know that the Courier has made such full and favorable notice of each day's proceedings. Our special thanks are due to Rev. James Lynch for sending us a copy of the report.

articles.headline: Notice: Minutes of the Philadelphia Annual Conference
articles.summary: The Minutes of the Philadelphia Annual Conference are now ready at our office, No. 619 Pine St. Price 15 cents. Persons out of town can have them sent to them, by mail, for 20 cents per copy. June 16, tf.

articles.headline: Notice: Quarterly Meetings of Frankford Circuit
articles.summary: The Quarterly Meetings of Frankford Circuit, will be held as follows: Frankford, 1st Sabbath in July; Harrisburg Hill, 2d; Ben Salem, 3d; Bristol, 4th. J. H. Smith, Elder in Charge. June 16, 2t.

articles.headline: Notice: First Quarterly Meeting of the Zion Mission Church
articles.summary: The First Quarterly Meeting of the Zion Mission Church, 7th street, below Dickerson, Philadelphia, Pa., will be held on June 25th, 1865, Providence permitting. At which time we expect to have several worthy divines to assist. H. J. Rhodes [VERIFY initials], Pastor.

articles.headline: Married
articles.summary: On the 11th of June, 1865, by Rev. William Moore, Mr. William T. Sample of Kaighnsville, N. J., to Miss Fanny Robinson [VERIFY], of Philadelphia, Pa. In Bristol, Pa., on the 15th inst. [VERIFY day], by Rev. M. Taylor, Mr. Samuel W. Stockton [VERIFY], late of Philadelphia, to Miss Martha Lena Conn [VERIFY], of Burlington, N. J. In this city, on Sunday evening, May 28th, by the Rev. Theo. Doughty Miller, Mr. Paul Moore, of Virginia, to Miss Josephine Woodson, of this city.

articles.headline: Obituary: Johnson
articles.summary: JOHNSON. Died, in Chicago, Illinois, at the house of Polly Thrailkills, Thomas Johnson of Co. I, 25th U. S. C. T., on June 10th, 1865. The deceased was a resident of this city, and should this meet the eye of his relatives, they are requested to call at the office of the Christian Recorder, and obtain some very valuable information.
people: deceased; Co. I, 25th U. S. C. T.; resident of Philadelphia

articles.headline: Gov. Curtin to the People of Pennsylvania
articles.summary: Executive Chamber, Harrisburg, June 10, 1865. To the People of Pennsylvania: The bloody struggle of four years is ended. The survivors are now returning to us; I recommend that in every part of the State, on the approaching anniversary of Independence, special observances be had of welcome to our returned defenders. Signed Andrew G. Curtin, Governor of Pennsylvania. (General; no colored regiment is named.)

articles.headline: Meeting of the South Carolina Conference
articles.summary: We copy the following report of the proceedings of the above named Conference from the columns of the Charleston Courier. We are much pleased and gratified to know that the Courier has made such full and favorable notice of each day's proceedings. Our special thanks are due to Rev. James Lynch for sending us a copy of the report.

articles.author: William A. K. Smith [VERIFY middle initial]
articles.summary: At the Annual Meeting of the District Grand Lodge, No. 2, of the I. O. of G. S. and D. of S. of the States of Pennsylvania and Delaware, held at the New Masonic Hall, South Eleventh street, Philadelphia, on Tuesday, June 6th, 1865, the following named brethren and sisters were duly elected and installed officers for the ensuing year. (The list runs over to the head of page 3.)

articles.headline: Festival
articles.summary: An entertainment was given by the Rev. S. T. Jones' Literary Society, at the Philadelphia Institute, on the 14th inst., for the benefit of the Missionary Fund of Wesley Church. Mr. Edward Evans, President of the Society, favored the audience with an address on 'The part the colored man has taken in the rebellion, and his rights as a citizen,' which was well received.

articles.headline: Unionville Correspondence
articles.summary: The true-hearted colored patriots of Unionville and vicinity, having somewhat recovered from the overwhelming stroke of sorrow so universally felt in consequence of the assassination of President Lincoln, determined to hold a meeting for the purpose of expressing their deep regret at our country's loss. The 27th of May arrived. The day was gloomy.

articles.headline: A Visit to the Public School in Brooklyn (in the editor's account of the New York and New England Conferences)
articles.summary: We paid a visit to the public school in Brooklyn, of which Mr. Dorsey, formerly of Philadelphia, is the talented Principal. There are three teachers in this school, including the Principal. The editor's account of the ending of the New York and New England Conferences fills the first three columns of the page.

articles.headline: Personal
articles.author: J. H. Turpin
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: On perusing your valuable paper a few days since, I saw an item relating to my appointment as a missionary to the Sunny South. Various circumstances compel me to defer my visit until another period. May the blessing of God go with Brothers Gibbs, Hedges and Thompson. Philadelphia, June 20, 1865.

articles.headline: Appointments for Indiana and Missouri Conferences; Episcopal Visits
articles.author: J. P. Campbell
articles.summary: The Indiana Conference will meet in Springfield, Illinois, on Saturday, August 19th, 1865. The Missouri Conference will meet in New Orleans, Louisiana, on Saturday, September 9, 1865. Episcopal visits: Cincinnati, Louisville, Nashville, Richmond, Indianapolis, Terre Haute, Chicago, Bloomington.

articles.headline: New York Conference Appointments; Appointments of the New England Conference
articles.summary: The following are the list of appointments made by the New York Annual Conference for the ensuing year: Bridge Street, James N. Williams; Fleet Street, J. Woodlyn; Sullivan Street, Henry Davis. The following brethren were transferred: Rev. R. H. Cain, South Carolina Conference; Revs. E. P. Gibbs [VERIFY initials], J. H. Hamilton, Wm. Watson and D. Seaton [VERIFY], Philadelphia Conference. From the New England Conference: Revs. W. W. Grimes, Jacob Mitchell, and W. S. Chase, to the Philadelphia Conference.

appointed to Sullivan Street, New York Conference

articles.headline: An Acknowledgment
articles.author: Wm. Offer
articles.summary: The undersigned takes great pleasure in acknowledging the following contributions from his friends and well-wishers, to aid him on his journey to California: Bethel Church, Philadelphia, $26.00; Mt. Zion, New Brunswick, 25.00; Mount Zion, Trenton, N. J., 16.50; Bethel, Burlington, N. J., 7.00; Germantown, 6.00.

articles.headline: Notice: Quarterly Meetings of Burlington Circuit; Excursion
articles.summary: The Quarterly Meetings of Burlington Circuit will be held as follows: At Mount Holly on the first Sabbath in July; at Burlington on the third Sabbath in July; at Evesham on the fourth Sabbath in July. T. Gould, Minister. Excursion: The Pearl street A. M. E. Sabbath school, of Burlington, N. J., will make an excursion on Thursday next, June 29th. There will be a festival held in the basement of the church in the evening. T. Gould, Minister.

articles.headline: Information Wanted: Thomas T. Marshall
articles.summary: Information wanted of Mr. Thomas T. Marshall. When last heard from he was in Mound City, Illinois, preparing to go to St. Louis, Missouri. His grandmother, Rebecca Thorn, died lately in Charleston, S. C., and it is desired that he should go home immediately, and settle the estate, as he is the oldest heir. Any information will be thankfully received by Mrs. Charlotte Washington, 1117 Rodman Street, Philadelphia, Pa. June 24, 2t.

articles.headline: Obituary: Veazey
articles.author: Margaret Williams
articles.summary: VEAZEY. Killed, at Deerfield, 15 miles from Salem, New Jersey, on Wednesday morning, June 14th, John Veazey, by the falling of a roof which he was engaged in raising. He was a fine young man, highly esteemed and beloved by all who knew him. He leaves a wife, mother and sister to mourn his untimely end.
people: deceased; killed at Deerfield, N. J. (printed 'Veazey' and 'Vessey')

articles.headline: Coal! Coal!! T. J. Bowers, Coal and Kindling Wood Depot, No. 634 Lombard Street
articles.summary: Coal! Coal!! Coal delivered to any part of the city, by large or small measure, by T. J. Bowers, Coal and Kindling Wood Depot, No. 634 Lombard Street. (Dated April 15.) T. J. Bowers is Thomas J. Bowers, the singer; 634 Lombard Street was also the address of the undertaking business of his sister, Mrs. Henrietta S. Duterte.
people: proprietor, Coal and Kindling Wood Depot, 634 Lombard Street

events.name: Social, Civil and Statistical Association -- closing lecture of the course by Hon. Wm. D. Kelley, Concert Hall
events.location: Concert Hall, Philadelphia
events.description: Report reprinted from the North American of the closing lecture of the course of the Social, Civil and Statistical Association (printed once as 'Society') at Concert Hall; no date is printed beyond 'last night'. The house was packed, the whites predominating. The band from Camp Wm. Penn, thirty musicians, gave the music. On the platform were clergymen of both colors, prominent among them Rev. Stephen Smith. Miss Greenfield, the Black Swan, sang, accompanying herself on the piano. Mr. Robert Purvis announced the speaker and, not being a member, thanked the Committee of Arrangements, of whom Mr. Wm. Still is chairman. Judge Kelley spoke fully two hours on 'The War, and the Rights of Humanity', arguing for equal civil and political rights and against recognizing the Louisiana state government.

events.name: Bethel A. M. E. Sabbath School -- 28th anniversary grand concert
events.location: Sansom Street Hall, Philadelphia
events.description: The Bethel A. M. E. Sabbath School will celebrate its 28th anniversary by a grand concert at Sansom Street Hall on Thursday evening, April 6. Mr. H. Shadd, conductor; Mr. F. M. Seymour, pianist; L. R. Seymour, Esq., general superintendent. Proceeds for the School Fund and the Soldiers' Aid Society. Cards of admission, 25 cts., at the A. M. E. Book Store, No. 619 Pine St.

events.name: Ladies' Union Association of Philadelphia -- distribution at the Summit House Hospital; visit to the army before Richmond planned
events.location: Summit House Hospital, Philadelphia
events.description: A committee of the Ladies' Union Association of Philadelphia (Misses Amelia E. and Annie R. Mills, and Miss Mary Burton, of Zoar church) distributed delicacies to the sick and wounded soldiers at the Summit House Hospital, bought with forty dollars given by the Ladies' Soldiers' Aid Association of Carlisle, Pa., and forwarded through Mr. Joseph C. Bustill (acknowledged by Amelia E. Mills, president, March 23, 1865). A committee of ladies will visit the army before Richmond in a week or two; contributions of bandages, farina, fruit, lint, etc. may be left with Miss A. E. Mills, President, Lombard street, above Tenth. Letter signed 'A Visitor', dated March 25th, 1865.

events.name: Funeral of Benjamin F. Brown, Principal of the Camden Colored School
events.location: No. 828 South Fourth street, Camden, N. J., to Johnson Cemetery
events.description: Benjamin F. Brown, Principal of the Camden Colored School, died on the 29th (March) in his thirty-third year. Members of Aurora Lodge, No. 9, A. Y. M., of the Grand Lodge of New Jersey, and of Mt. Zion Tabernacle, I. O. of B. and S. of L. and C., were invited to attend the funeral on Sunday, April 2d, from his late residence, No. 828 South Fourth street, Camden, to Johnson Cemetery.

events.name: Rejoicing and grand illumination in Philadelphia on the fall of Richmond
events.location: Philadelphia
events.description: On Monday (April 3) the news of the fall of Richmond reached the city; the Old State House Bell pealed and people laid aside work. In the evening there was a grand illumination, shared by the colored citizens: the Institute for Colored Youth, the rooms of the Delmonico Assembly, and several other gathering places of the colored people were illuminated, and private residences showed lanterns and American flags. The rejoicing went on through Thursday ('Babylon is fallen'). A companion editorial, 'The Union Victories', gives all praise to the colored troops, 'the first to enter the doomed city'. No persons are named.

events.name: Ladies' Union Association and Sanitary Committee of St. Thomas' Protestant Episcopal Church -- deputation leaves for City Point
events.location: Philadelphia, for City Point, Va.
events.description: A deputation from the Ladies' Union Association and the Sanitary Committee of St. Thomas' Protestant Episcopal Church left Philadelphia on Thursday morning (April 6) with needed articles to relieve the sufferers around City Point and in the hospitals in the vicinity. No members are named.

events.name: John Wesley M. E. Church -- Quarterly Meeting
events.location: John Wesley M. E. Church, Shippen St., above 7th, Philadelphia
events.description: Quarterly Meeting on Sabbath, April 9, 1865. Preaching at half-past ten by the Rev. Stanford, at three o'clock by Rev. Elder Moore, followed by the Lord's Supper; Rev. H. Henson to officiate at half-past seven in the evening. Rev. Abraham Brown, Pastor.

events.name: Harriet Tubman lectures to the 24th U. S. C. T. at Camp William Penn
events.location: Camp William Penn, Chelton Hills, Pa.
events.description: Letter of 'A. H.', Chelton Hills, April 6, 1865. On Saturday evening (April 1) 'a colored woman, known as Harriet Tubman', 'the great Underground Rail Road woman', gave a 'homespun lecture' in her own language to the soldiers of the 24th regiment, U. S. C. T., now at the camp, with a thrilling account of her trials in the South during the past three years among the contrabands and colored soldiers. The regiment passed resolutions to be published in the Recorder; Professors Burris and Turner presided at the organ; a liberal collection was taken for the lecturer. On Sunday, April 2, the chaplain, Henry Anstice [VERIFY], preached on the Atonement. On Monday about 3 o'clock, with the 24th drawn up for battalion drill, Col. Wagner read a dispatch that Richmond had fallen and that the colored troops who had left Camp Wm. Penn were the first to enter the city, to indescribable shouts. On Tuesday the Post Band paraded through Jenkintown. On Wednesday Company B presented First Lieutenant Whitelock with a sword, through Capt. Cox. Mrs. Mears teaches the soldiers two nights a week and on Sunday, and plans a permanent institution and home for disabled and wounded colored soldiers in the county of Philadelphia.

events.name: Philadelphia rejoices at Lee's surrender
events.location: Philadelphia
events.description: Editorial 'Richmond Captured': Lee has surrendered; 'for the past week Philadelphia has represented a grand carnival'. The editor hopes the rejoicing will not be followed by some proclamation or act against 'the most loyal race of people of which the government can boast'. The companion piece, 'Prejudice Not Yet Dead', corrects last week's claim: the colored troops were in the advance on Richmond but were ordered to halt until the white troops arrived and were given the advance. The date given here is the day the news reached the city (the surrender was April 9); the paper prints no day. No persons are named.

events.name: Soldiers' Musical Temperance Union -- grand Temperance Concert
events.location: Sansom Street Hall, Philadelphia
events.description: The Soldiers' Musical Temperance Union will give a grand Temperance Concert at Sansom Street Hall on Tuesday evening, April 25th, for the benefit of the cause among the Volunteers. Tickets 25 cts., at 1014 Market St., 1322 Chestnut St., 18 North Seventh St., and Gould's, Seventh and Chestnut, and at the door. No officers are named.

events.name: Bethel A. M. E. Sabbath School -- twenty-eighth anniversary concert (report)
events.location: Sansom Street Hall, Philadelphia
events.description: On Thursday evening, April 6th, the Sabbath school attached to the Bethel A. M. E. Church celebrated its twenty-eighth anniversary with a grand concert in Sansom Street Hall, 'a decided success'; solos, quartettes and choruses, with about a hundred voices in working order. The pecuniary result was not yet known. No names are given in the report (the officers are in the notice of April 1).

events.name: National Equal Rights League -- Executive Board meets at its headquarters in Philadelphia
events.location: National Equal Rights Bureau, South 7th Street, Philadelphia (number not legible)
events.description: The Executive Board of the National Equal Rights League met at its headquarters in Philadelphia on March 10 and by adjournment on March 14, 1865, at 12 o'clock. Present: J. Mercer Langston, President; Ransom Harris, Esq., of Nashville, Tenn.; and St. George R. Taylor and Davis D. Turner, the Secretaries. The Board reported State Leagues organized since November 24 in Louisiana, North Carolina, Tennessee, Missouri, Michigan, Ohio, Pennsylvania and Massachusetts, with New York to meet in convention, and appealed to colored men everywhere to form auxiliary leagues and pay funds through the Secretaries. Signed John Mercer Langston, President; St. George R. Taylor and Davis D. Turner, Secretaries; office on South 7th Street, Phila.

events.name: Procession of the colored people of Philadelphia and presentation of colors to the 24th U. S. C. T. at the State House
events.location: In front of the State House (Independence Hall), Philadelphia
events.description: Friday, April 14, 1865. Two items report the day. (1) 'The Procession of Friday Last' is almost wholly illegible on the film: what can be read is that the colored people of Philadelphia paraded on 'last Friday', that the Delmonico Assembly, No. 1, formed one of the leading features of the parade, and that the whole was under the direction of 'Mr. J. F. G..., Sr.' (surname illegible) assisted by a large number of deputy marshals, among them a Sergeant-Major of a U. S. C. T. regiment and a 'Mr. W. E. ...' (names illegible). (2) 'Presentation of Colors to the 24th Regt. U. S. C. T.' is legible in its first half and is the source of everything that follows. At noon the 24th United States Colored Troops, Lieutenant Colonel Trippe commanding, followed by various civic organizations, were drawn up before the State House. A meeting was organized with Mr. J. C. White, Jr., as President; Messrs. Jos. Le Count, Jos. C. Bustill, Richard Gleaves, Clayton Miller and Chas. Simpson as Vice Presidents; and W. H. Minton, Secretary. After prayer by Rev. H. H. Garnet, of Washington, the President introduced Mr. O. V. Catto, who presented a regimental flag 'gotten up under the auspices of the Banneker Institute by contributions from the public'. The President's introduction places the meeting 'at the very moment when the gallant Anderson is raising the Stars and Stripes over Fort Sumter'. The paper gives only 'a few of the points' of Catto's speech; the legible part speaks of the plan of reconstruction and of the votes of the blacks. From that point to the foot of the column the report is illegible on the film (the reply for the regiment and the close cannot be read). The shorter item says, as far as it can be read, that the regiment then left for Camp Wm. Penn with the flag.
attendees: president of the meeting (printed J. C. White, Jr.)
offered prayer (printed Rev. H. H. Garnet, of Washington)

events.name: Ladies' Union Association -- special meeting on the death of President Lincoln
events.location: Philadelphia
events.description: At a special meeting of the Ladies' Union Association held Saturday evening, April 15th, a committee was appointed to draw up resolutions on the death of the President. The resolutions deplore the loss of him 'who has with wonderful ability brought us safely thus far'; call Lincoln a bright Christian example and first in the hearts of his countrymen; declare no sympathy for those ready 'to grasp the hands already red with the blood of the noblest sons of our land'; recognize in the murder 'another offspring of the monster slavery' and its twin, Prejudice; call for a rigorous execution of justice on the leaders of the rebellion and support for President Andrew Johnson; extend sympathy to the family and Cabinet; and resolve that the Fair to be opened at Concert Hall, April 17th, for sick and wounded colored soldiers, be postponed on account of the great national calamity. Committee: S. Louise Iredell, Carrie R. LeCount, Mary A. Brown [VERIFY] and a fourth name too faint to read.

events.name: Ladies' Union Association -- amateur concert
events.location: Sansom Street Hall, Philadelphia
events.description: The amateur concert of the Ladies' Union Association, Monday evening, April 24th, at Sansom Street Hall; doors open at 7 1/2, concert at 8 precisely; tickets 25 cents. The editor (page 2) expects it to be one of the most successful of the season. No performers are named in the notice.

events.name: Independent Order of Good Samaritans and Daughters of Samaria (a Pennsylvania Lodge) -- Fair postponed
events.location: Philadelphia (hall not legible)
events.description: A Fair that was to have been held during the week from April 17th by a Pennsylvania Lodge of the Independent Order of Good Samaritans and Daughters of Samaria is postponed until May, in consequence of the national calamity. The lodge number, the hall and the new date are too faint to read [VERIFY]. No officers are named.

events.name: Philadelphia Annual Conference of the A. M. E. Church -- session called
events.location: Union Church, Coates street, Philadelphia
events.description: Bishop A. W. Wayman's notice, dated Baltimore, April 19, 1865: the Philadelphia Annual Conference of the A. M. E. Church will meet in the Union Church, Coates street, Philadelphia, on Saturday, May 13th, 1865. Candidates for admission and orders are to meet the Committee for Examination the day before the Conference convenes. An editorial note on page 2 asks all the brethren to observe the notice.

events.name: Literary Association of the Philadelphia Annual Conference of the A. M. E. Church -- meeting called
events.location: Bethel Church, Philadelphia (the notice appears to read 'in the basement of Bethel Church' [VERIFY])
events.description: The Literary Association of the Philadelphia Annual Conference of the A. M. E. Church is requested to meet at Bethel Church on Wednesday morning, May 10th, at 9 o'clock. By order of the President, Peter Gardiner. The secretary's name is printed faintly: Rev. H. W. Winder [VERIFY]. The notice is marked to run twice.

events.name: Ladies' Union Association -- Fair postponed on account of the death of President Lincoln
events.location: Philadelphia (place of the Fair not stated in the notice)
events.description: Notice headed 'We mourn, our Chief has fallen.' On account of the national calamity the Fair of the Ladies' Union Association is postponed until the 1[?]th of May [VERIFY: the day is not legible]; tickets already issued will be good for that time; the Fair will continue two weeks. By order of the President; S. Lizzie Brown, Sec'y. A postscript returns the thanks of the Association to the Ladies' Union Association of Harrisburg for a donation and to Miss Amelia Williams [VERIFY] for money collected in Harrisburg, signed by the President, Miss E. M[...] [VERIFY: surname not legible] and S. L. Brown, Secretary.

events.name: Frankford -- memorial meeting for President Lincoln at the A. M. E. church
events.location: A. M. E. church, Frankford
events.description: Letter dated Frankford, April 1[9], 1865 (the printed day is unclear; April 19 was the day of the national obsequies ordered by the Secretary of State). The church was opened for the sympathizing friends of the late Abraham Lincoln. The United Daughters of America, No. 2, the United Benevolent Daughters of Davis [VERIFY name], and the Equal Rights League of the first district of Philadelphia formed in procession and proceeded to the church. Rev. Henderson Davis opened with singing and prayer and spoke; Mr. Henderson Davis, Jr. spoke next; Mr. Jo[...] Trusty, Esq. [VERIFY given name] was the third speaker; Rev. Samuel Murray closed, saying that as God placed Joshua in Moses' stead so He would place Andrew Johnson in Abraham Lincoln's stead, and gave out a hymn. Benediction by Rev. Henderson Davis. Signed by a committee: Lewis N. B[...] [VERIFY surname], H. Davis, Jr., J. G. Lee [VERIFY], Wm. S. Walker.

events.name: Camp William Penn -- Thanksgiving, Easter and Lincoln memorial services (24th U.S.C.T.)
events.location: Camp William Penn, Chelton Hill, Pa.
events.description: Letter signed A. B., Chelton Hill, April 21st, 1865. Sunday, April 9th, the day of Thanksgiving: the chaplain, Rev. Henry Austier [VERIFY spelling], read Governor Curtin's Proclamation; in the evening Rev. B. Faucett [VERIFY] preached from Hebrews 12: 1, 2; about midnight the cry was heard in camp that Lee and his whole army had surrendered. Easter Sunday, April 16th: Rev. Dr. Parvin preached on the Resurrection and compared the death of the Saviour to the martyrdom of the President. Wednesday morning, April 19th: Col. Wagner had the War Department orders on the obsequies read to the 24th regiment U. S. colored troops by Adjutant Milliken [VERIFY], and Dr. Parvin preached on the life and death of Abraham Lincoln, saying the time had come when soldiers, white and black, were known only as soldiers.

events.name: A. M. E. Zion Mission Sabbath School -- Great Exhibition
events.location: Zion Church, Seventh street below Dickerson, Philadelphia
events.description: Editorial notice: a Great Exhibition of the A. M. E. Zion Mission Sabbath School is to be given on Wednesday evening, the 10th instant, at the Zion Church in Seventh street below Dickerson. The paper asks the citizens to encourage and sustain 'Rev. Brother Winder, the pastor over the school' (surname only as printed).

events.name: Bethel Church -- last Quarterly Meeting of the Conference year
events.location: Bethel Church, Philadelphia
events.description: The last Quarterly Meeting for Bethel church for the Conference year was held 'last Sabbath' (April 30, 1865). Rev. William Moore is now the pastor and has had a revival during the last month. The General Class met on Friday night and the Love Feast was observed on Monday night. A number of white friends of different denominations (Methodists, Presbyterians and Baptists) were present.

events.name: Institute for Colored Youth -- thirteenth Annual Commencement
events.location: Institute for Colored Youth, Philadelphia
events.description: The thirteenth Annual Commencement of the Institute took place 'on last Thursday, and continued till Friday night' (May 4 and 5, 1865). The editor credits Professor Bassett and his corps of teachers. No class list is printed in this issue.

events.name: Philadelphia Annual Conference of the A. M. E. Church -- annual and missionary sermons announced
events.location: Conference at Union Church, Coates street; the sermons at Bethel Church on Sixth street, Philadelphia
events.description: Bishop A. W. Wayman's second notice, dated May 1st, 1865: the Conference meets in the Union Church, Coates street, on Saturday, May 13th, 1865. The annual sermon to the Conference will be preached on Monday afternoon, May 15th, at 4 o'clock, by Rev. Henry Davis; the Missionary sermon on Thursday afternoon, May 18th, at 4 o'clock, by Rev. Joshua A. Woodlyn (as printed). Both services in Bethel Church on Sixth street. The examining committees are to meet the candidates the day before the Conference convenes.

events.name: James H. Teagle's first Grand Concert
events.location: Concert Hall (Philadelphia; city not stated in the notice)
events.description: Notice: James H. Teagle's first Grand Concert on Monday evening, May 8th, at Concert Hall, with two grand pianos from Chickering & Sons. Artists: Madam Brown; A. S. Purnell; W. F. Sturgis, New York; J. D. Cliff; and J. H. Teagle.
attendees: gives the concert; pianist (also printed J. H. Teagle)

events.name: Ladies' Union Association -- Fair postponed to May 15 on account of the death of President Lincoln
events.location: Philadelphia (place of the Fair not stated in the notice)
events.description: Notice headed 'We mourn, our Chief has fallen' (first printed April 29; this is the clearer impression). The Fair of the Ladies' Union Association is postponed until the 15th of May; tickets already issued will be good; the Fair will continue two weeks. By order of the President; S. Lizzie Brown, Sec'y. Postscript: the Association thanks the Ladies' Union Association of Harrisburg for their donation of $40, and Miss Amelia Williams for $60 collected in Harrisburg. Miss E. Mills, President; S. L. Brown, Secretary.

events.name: A. M. E. Church at Eversham, New Jersey -- laying of the corner stone
events.location: Eversham, New Jersey (as printed; Evesham)
events.description: The corner stone of the new A. M. E. Church at Eversham, New Jersey, is to be laid on Thursday, May 18th, 1865, exercises to commence at 2 o'clock P. M. Bishop Wayman and other ministers are expected. The church hopes to raise $100 on the occasion. Signed T. Gould, Minister in charge.

events.name: Philadelphia Annual Conference of the A. M. E. Church -- forty-ninth session, first three days
events.location: A. M. E. Union Church, Coates street, near Fifth, Philadelphia
events.description: First day (Saturday, May 13, 1865, 9 A.M.): Bishop Wayman presiding, assisted by Rev. Wm. P. Quinn, senior Bishop. Elder Moore led in prayer. Rev. J. Woodlyn appointed Secretary and Brother W. W. Winder assistant Secretary. Rev. Benjamin Lynch, transferred from the Ohio Conference, and Revs. N. A. Turpen, Geo. E. Boyer, W. H. Williams and H. J. Rhodes, from the Baltimore Annual Conference, were confirmed as members. Standing committees appointed; examination of characters until one o'clock. Rev. E. Weaver, editor of the Christian Recorder, appointed reporter for the daily newspapers. Second day (Monday, May 15): Bishop Quinn in the chair; religious services by Rev. John H. Henson and A. C. Cuppen (as printed); committee reports; brethren offered for membership referred to the Committee on Membership; financial reports; at 4 P.M. adjourned to hear the annual sermon by Rev. Henry Davis; the Missionary sermon announced for Bethel Church on Thursday the 18th by Rev. Joshua Woodlyn. Third day (Tuesday, May 16): Bishop Wayman presiding, assisted by Bishop Quinn; the complaint against Rev. Brother Jay withdrawn; the application of Rev. Brother J. H. Smith for confirmation to membership withdrawn; Isaiah Broaden, admitted last year, dropped from the roll for leaving his circuit without notifying the Bishop; Brothers Thos. H. Cooper, John C. Cornish and W. W. Winder elected to Elders' orders; Revs. J. G. Beulah and Sheppard Holcomb continued on the superannuated list. Bishop Campbell, just back from California (he arrived Monday evening the 15th), walked up the aisle and took his seat on the platform. Adjourned to Wednesday at 9 o'clock. The appointments are not printed in this issue.
attendees: senior Bishop; assisted, and presided on the second day
Secretary (Rev.; also printed Joshua Woodlyn); Missionary sermon

events.name: Dumas Dramatic Association -- meeting on the death of its President, Junius H. Purnell
events.location: the Association's room, Philadelphia (address not given)
events.description: At a meeting of the Dumas Dramatic Association held at their room on Thursday evening, May 11th, 1865, a preamble and resolutions were adopted on the death of 'our beloved President and companion, Junius H. Purnell' [VERIFY given name: the small capitals are blurred]: sympathy with the bereaved parents of the deceased; the members to wear a badge of mourning for thirty days; the proceedings to be sent to the parents and published in the Sunday Despatch and Christian Recorder; the Association to attend the funeral in a body. Signed Joseph C. Davis, Vice Pres.; Robert J. H. Johnson, Treas.; James E. Harris, Secretary. Dated Philadelphia, May 12th, 1865.

events.name: Philadelphia Annual Conference of the A. M. E. Church -- forty-ninth session, May 17 to 23, and the appointments for 1865-66
events.location: A. M. E. Union Church, Coates street, Philadelphia
events.description: Wednesday May 17: Bishop Wayman in the chair; services by Rev. Wm. W. Grimes of the New England Conference; Revs. James Hamilton (New York Conference), W. W. Grimes and J. Mitchell (New England Conference) introduced; two local preachers of the Zion Mission church elected to Deacon's orders if they stand examination; the death of Rev. F. T. Hall, local preacher of the A. M. E. Union Church, laid before Conference. Thursday May 18: services by Rev. Joseph H. Smith; the Editor and General Book Steward made his annual report; Bishop Wayman, called away to lay the corner stone of a new church in the Burlington Circuit, placed Rev. Thomas Henry in the chair; the Committee on Ordination reported in favor of ordaining four deacons. Friday May 19: Bishops Wayman, Quinn and Campbell; services by Rev. Wm. H. Chase of the New England District; Bishop Campbell asked Conference for a man for California. Saturday May 20: services by Rev. Theodore Gould; report on the Book Concern adopted; on the report of the Committee on the State of the Country the speakers were Rev. Mr. Flannery, agent of the Methodist Tract Society of Philadelphia, Rev. J. Mitchell, Rev. Wm. H. Jones of Canada and Rev. Stephen Smith; laid over on motion of Elisha Weaver. Monday May 22: services by Rev. N. H. Turpin; a resolution of condolence 'with the widow of the late Andrew Till' offered by E. Weaver (see the death notice on page 3, which names the wife as the deceased); on the State of the Country Elisha Weaver, Mr. Isaiah Weare, Friend Hood [VERIFY], Rev. Mr. Patterson of the M. E. Church, Rev. Mr. Cookman, pastor of the M. E. Church on Fourth street between Market and Arch, Brother Mitchell and Bishop Campbell spoke, and the report was adopted unanimously. The Conference then sat as a Missionary Society and elected: President, Rev. Stephen Smith; Vice President, Rev. Wm. Moore; Secretary, Elisha Weaver; Treasurer, Rev. J. P. B. Eddy; Executive Committee, Revs. Joseph Eddy, Nelson A. Turpen, James Hollin, James Frisby, Benj. Lynch, R. P. Gibbs, Joseph H. Smith and Wm. Williams; dues paid in, $27. Tuesday May 23: thanks to The Press for publishing the daily proceedings; total Missionary money collected $940.97 [VERIFY first digit]; $250 to be sent to Bro. Davis at Baltimore. THE APPOINTMENTS AS PRINTED: Philadelphia, Pa.: A. M. E. Union Church, to be supplied; Bethel Church, W. Moore; Wesley Church, to be supplied; Zion Mission, H. J. Rhodes; West Philadelphia, to be supplied; West Chester circuit, James V. Pierce; Reading circuit, T. A. Cuff; Downingtown circuit, E. Laws [VERIFY initial]; Danville circuit, to be supplied; Lancaster circuit, J. Young; Chester and Horntown, P. Gardner; Oxford circuit, J. W. Turpin; Bridgeton, to be supplied; Cape May circuit, John C. Cornish; Burlington circuit, T. Gould; Bordentown circuit, James Hollen; Trenton station, Thos. H. Cooper; Princeton station, to be supplied; New Brunswick, B. Lynch; Freehold circuit, A. C. Crippen. Delaware: Wilmington, to be supplied; Lewistown, John H. Henson; Frederick, W. H. Williams; Smyrna, Gilbert Waters; Camden, Harrison Lewis; Milton, Wm. H. Turner; Penningtonville, Wm. R. Norris. Transferred: Henry Davis, Joshua Woodlyn, W. W. Winder, and Wm. Rodgers, to New York Conference; A. L. Stanford and T. Steward, to South Carolina Conference; Redman Faucet, to Missouri Conference; Rev. Thomas W. Henry to Baltimore Conference. E. Weaver was elected District Book Steward. The next session is to meet at Princeton, New Jersey, on the second Saturday in May, 1866.

events.name: Missionary Society of the Philadelphia Annual Conference -- election of officers
events.location: A. M. E. Union Church, Coates street, Philadelphia
events.description: On Monday, May 22, 1865, the Conference resolved itself into a Missionary Society, altered its constitution to harmonize with that of the Parent Missionary Society, and elected officers for the ensuing year: President, Rev. Stephen Smith; Vice President, Rev. Wm. Moore; Secretary, Elisha Weaver; Treasurer, Rev. J. P. B. Eddy; Executive Committee, Revs. Joseph Eddy, Nelson A. Turpen, James Hollin, James Frisby, Benj. Lynch, R. P. Gibbs, Joseph H. Smith, and Wm. Williams. Bros. Stephen Smith and Moore were installed; members enrolled and paid dues to the amount of $27. The Society met again on Tuesday the 23d: cash receipts $36 [VERIFY]; total Missionary money collected $940.97 [VERIFY first digit].
attendees: President, Conference Missionary Society (Rev.); spoke on the State of the Country
Secretary, Conference Missionary Society; elected District Book Steward (also printed E. Weaver)

events.name: Anniversary of the Sabbath schools of the city churches
events.location: Bethel church, Philadelphia
events.description: The anniversary of the Sabbath schools connected with the different churches in the city took place on Monday, May 22, 1865, in the Bethel church, which was crowded. Addresses by Revs. Stephen Smith, Turpen and Woodlyn. Dr. Armstrong made a short speech and presented a silk banner to the Sabbath school class which had collected the most Missionary money: the infant class of Bethel Church, under the charge of Miss Esther Armstrong. The Doctor promised a like present next year. The Bethel Sabbath school, through its superintendent (not named), contributed $50 [VERIFY amount] to the Missionary cause.
attendees: teacher in charge of the Bethel infant class (Miss)

events.name: Visit of the Conference to the Old Folks' Home
events.location: Old Folks' Home, Front street, between Spruce and Pine, Philadelphia
events.description: On Saturday evening, May 20, 1865, the Conference visited the Old Folks' Home on Front street between Spruce and Pine, established to care for aged colored people and managed by a white and colored Board of Directors. The visitors were received by brother Morris Hall and the matron (a white woman, not named), were shown through the apartments, and had prayer with the inmates.

events.name: South Carolina Conference of the A.M.E. Church: first annual session at Charleston (second to fifth days)
events.location: Zion church, Calhoun street, Charleston, S.C.
events.description: Reprinted from the Charleston Courier, sent by Rev. James Lynch. The Conference met at Zion church, Calhoun street, Charleston, Bishop D. A. Payne presiding; religious services by Rev. R. H. Cain. Charles Bradwell of the Savannah Quarterly Conference was admitted into the itinerancy; local preachers were admitted and several men were elected to orders, among them Theophilus G. Steward and Jas. H. A. Johnson (the rest of these lists is too faint on the film to read with certainty). Rev. James Lynch offered resolutions on the educational work among the freedmen, thanking the American Missionary Association and the N. F. R. Association; he reported as chairman of the Committee on Missions. Rev. James A. Handy offered resolutions on the assassination of President Lincoln. Rev. R. H. Cain offered resolutions denying that the A.M.E. Church draws a distinction of color or excludes whites. Resolutions were passed to join in celebrating the first half century of the A.M.E. Church in April 1866. Stations and circuits were laid out: Savannah City Station (Union A.M.E. Church, formerly Andrew Chapel, and Wesley Chapel), Charleston City Station, Raleigh, Wilmington, Hilton Head, Beaufort River Circuit, Edisto and others. The printed list of appointments is too faint to read on this film. All persons named are missionaries and Southern preachers, not Philadelphians.

events.name: Two colored carpet cleaners killed by a locomotive at Washington Avenue; coroner's jury delays its verdict
events.location: Washington Avenue crossing, Philadelphia
events.description: On Thursday, May 25, 1865, five old colored residents of Philadelphia, returning in a wagon from a day's work cleaning a load of carpets, were struck at a crossing on Washington Avenue (cross street printed faintly, read as 15th [VERIFY]) by a locomotive of the Philadelphia, Wilmington and Baltimore Railroad running without cars. Horace Potter, 'who is well known in our midst', saw the locomotive and jumped. The two men seated at the rear of the wagon, Wm. Rhodes and Alexander Thompson, jumped or were thrown out and the locomotive passed over their bodies. The driver and Horace Potter and one Thos. (surname unreadable) were uninjured. The Recorder complains that the coroner's jury had not yet given a verdict, says no bell or signal was given, and rejects a daily paper's charge that the men were intoxicated: 'their sobriety can be vouched for by hundreds of our citizens'. The death notice on page 3 reads: 'Killed, by being run over by a locomotive of the Philadelphia, Wilmington & Baltimore Railroad, on the 25th day of May, William Rhodes and Alex. Thompson, both old residents of Philadelphia.'

events.name: Rev. William Offer preaches at Bethel Church before sailing for California
events.location: Bethel Church, Philadelphia
events.description: Notice: Rev. William Offer, who intends sailing for California shortly, will preach in Bethel church on Sabbath next (June 4, 1865) at 3 P. M.

events.name: Colored people's Educational Monument to Abraham Lincoln: officers selected
events.location: Washington, D.C.
events.description: An Educational Monument to the memory of Abraham Lincoln is to be erected by the colored people at Washington. Officers as printed: President, Rev. H. H. Garnet; Vice President, James Wormley; Treasurer, Rev. Stephen Smith; Assistant, Walker Lewis; Recording Secretary, Mr. Lewis A. Bell; Corresponding Secretary, William J. Wilson. Only Rev. Stephen Smith is a Philadelphian; the others are of Washington and are given in the text only.

events.name: Bishop Campbell on the street cars (lecture 'The War and Its Issues', San Francisco)
events.location: Powell street African M. E. church, San Francisco
events.description: In his lecture at the Powell street African M. E. church, San Francisco, reprinted June 3, 1865, Bishop Campbell counted among the gains of the war that colored people were now allowed to testify in the courts and, in Washington and Alexandria, to ride in the street cars. He believed they had been allowed that privilege in San Francisco by Judge Pratt's decision. He told how he got on a car in Washington before colored people had been allowed by law to ride in the cars of that city, and heard the conductor and driver say that if the bill then in Congress ever passed there would be a rebellion in Washington: 'A rebellion to be inaugurated by drivers and conductors of street cars! The law passed, but who ever heard of the threatened rebellion?' He had travelled from Washington to Baltimore and from Baltimore to Philadelphia without a pass. No Philadelphia car item appears in this issue; this is the only street car passage in the four June issues.

events.name: Penn Temperance Association: Emancipation Jubilee at Darby
events.location: Town Hall, Darby, Pa.
events.description: The members of the Penn Temperance Association gave an Emancipation Jubilee in Town Hall, Darby (Delaware County, Pa.) on a Thursday evening (date not given; the letter is printed June 10, 1865). The hall was crowded and a number of white friends attended. After singing and prayer a fac-simile of the Emancipation Proclamation and a portrait of the late President were presented to the Association, the first by Georgianna Thompson [VERIFY] and the second by E. Y. Dingle [VERIFY]. Isaac Carr [VERIFY] was the first speaker; the next was Samuel Thompson [VERIFY], a young man who had never before appeared in public; George Sanford [VERIFY] spoke on 'The Rebellion is Ended'. A colored soldier from the army and E. Y. Dingle [VERIFY] followed. A party of singers from Philadelphia furnished the music. A collection was taken up for the Presidential Monument. The print is very faint on the film and no name in this item could be read with certainty; none is linked.

events.name: Bethel A.M.E. Church: class of Rev. J. Frisby presents him a gold headed cane
events.location: Bethel A. M. E. Church, Philadelphia
events.description: On Friday evening, May 26, 1865, a portion of the class under Rev. J. Frisby of Bethel A. M. E. Church presented him with a gold headed cane, valued at about $57 [VERIFY]. The presentation speeches were made by Mrs. E. Evans and Miss E. Lancaster on behalf of the donors. The names of the donors as printed: Elizabeth Evans, Diana Bristo [VERIFY], Emma Lancaster, Rebecca Turner, Rachel Cassidy [VERIFY], Mrs. ---- Davis, Mary Brown, Annie Peters, Rachel Green, Miss ---- Chew, Hannah Turner, Henry Clark, Wm. Stokes, J. Fountain, W. Thompson, S. Evans, Mr. ---- Daniels, Frances Valentine, Charlotte Bostic [VERIFY], J. Thompson, Mary Gibson, Charlotte Stevens.

events.name: Union Baptist Church (Minster St.): day of mourning service for President Lincoln and collection for the Lincoln Monument Fund
events.location: Union Baptist Church, Minster St. between Lombard and Pine Sts., above Sixth street, Philadelphia
events.description: On Thursday, June 1, 1865, the day appointed by President Johnson's proclamation, the colored citizens of Philadelphia who are members of the Union Baptist Church, 'located in Minster St., between Lombard and Pine Sts., above Sixth street', met in their place of worship. Though few were present, after prayers they lifted a collection of $8.31 [VERIFY amount], which they sent to Mayor Alexander Henry to be deposited in the Lincoln Monument Fund, with an address. Signed by the Committee: Joseph Washington, John Boling [VERIFY], James Felix [VERIFY], Reuben Coots [VERIFY].

events.name: Unity Lodge, No. 711, Grand United Order of Odd Fellows: twenty-first anniversary and Grand Demonstration
events.location: Sansom Street Hall, Philadelphia
events.description: The twenty-first anniversary of Unity Lodge, No. 711, of the Grand United Order of Odd Fellows, and of the introduction of the Order into the State of Pennsylvania, to be celebrated at the Sansom Street Hall on Wednesday evening, June 14, 1865. Addresses to be delivered by the Grand Master of the Order, Brother James McC. Crummill [VERIFY spelling], P. G. M.; Brother David B. Bowser, P. G. M.; Brother Charles F. Jones [VERIFY middle initial], P. G. M. Brother Charles B. Colly [VERIFY] will preside. A silver-plated ice pitcher will be presented to the member of the Ladies' Committee selling the largest number of tickets. Tickets 75 cents, to be had of the Committee; the editor's notice on page 2 names Mrs. James W. Brown, Shippen street, as one of the committee selling tickets.

events.location: Frankford, Philadelphia
events.description: Quarterly meetings of the Frankford Circuit: Frankford, first Sabbath in July (July 2, 1865); Harrisburg Hill, second Sabbath; Ben Salem, third Sabbath; Bristol, fourth Sabbath. Signed J. H. Smith, Elder in Charge (confirmed on the June 24 printing).

events.name: Zion Mission Church, 7th street below Dickerson: first quarterly meeting
events.location: Zion Mission Church, 7th street below Dickerson, Philadelphia
events.description: The First Quarterly Meeting of the Zion Mission Church, 7th street, below Dickerson, Philadelphia, to be held on June 25, 1865, with several divines expected to assist. Signed H. J. Rhodes [VERIFY initials], Pastor.

events.name: Rev. S. T. Jones' Literary Society: entertainment for the Missionary Fund of Wesley Church
events.location: Philadelphia Institute, Philadelphia
events.description: An entertainment given by the Rev. S. T. Jones' Literary Society at the Philadelphia Institute (Lombard Street above Seventh) on June 14, 1865, for the benefit of the Missionary Fund of Wesley Church. Mr. Edward Evans, President of the Society, gave an address on 'The part the colored man has taken in the rebellion, and his rights as a citizen'. Music: Mr. Joseph Freeman presided at the melodeon, and popular songs were given by members of the society and others. The whole was under the management of Mr. C. E. Evans; the assemblage dispersed at 12 o'clock. Amount realized, $45.50.

events.name: Unionville (Chester County): colored citizens' two-day memorial meeting for President Lincoln
events.location: A. M. E. Church, Unionville, Chester County, Pa.
events.description: A meeting of the colored people of Unionville and vicinity on Saturday, May 27, 1865, moved from the grove to the A. M. E. Church because of rain; called to order by the President and Chief Marshal of the day, Speakman Miller. Rev. Jno. W. Stevenson, of Oxford Circuit, made the opening address; Geo. Morris, Esq., Rev. Wm. D. Johnson of Ashmun Institute and others delivered eulogies. The meeting continued on the Sabbath (May 28): Rev. Jno. W. Stevenson presided, Rev. Wm. D. Johnson prayed, and the author and traveller Bayard Taylor addressed the meeting and read a communication from the late President on the education of the freedmen; P. P. Hodges of Ashmun Institute spoke; the afternoon orator was John Stebbins, M. D. In the evening Rev. Wm. D. Johnson preached in the A. M. E. Church, followed by Rev. John W. Stevenson, the former pastor. Chester County names are given in the text only, except the Philadelphia Conference minister.

events.name: New York and New England Conferences: ministers transferred to the Philadelphia Conference
events.description: Printed with the appointment lists of the two conferences (June 1865). From the New York Conference: Rev. R. H. Cain transferred to the South Carolina Conference; Revs. E. P. Gibbs [VERIFY initials], J. H. Hamilton, Wm. Watson and D. Seaton [VERIFY] to the Philadelphia Conference. From the New England Conference: Rev. G. H. Rue to the Baltimore Conference, and Revs. W. W. Grimes, Jacob Mitchell and W. S. Chase to the Philadelphia Conference. Former Philadelphia ministers in the New York list: J. Woodlyn (Fleet Street), Henry Davis (Sullivan Street), John Frisby (Westchester circuit; first letters faint). Rev. H. J. Johnson presides over the New England missions.

events.name: Contributions of the Philadelphia district churches for Rev. Wm. Offer's journey to California
events.description: Wm. Offer acknowledges contributions to aid him on his journey to California: Bethel Church, Philadelphia, $26.00; Mt. Zion, New Brunswick, $25.00; Mount Zion, Trenton, N. J., $16.50; Bethel, Burlington, N. J., $7.00; Germantown, $6.00; Salem, N. J., $5.00; Pennington, N. events.location: Pearl street A. M. E. Church, Burlington, N. J.
